scope: Prioritized findings reviewed at source and application boundary; remaining library dismissals are inventoried for individual call-site review, not declared safe.

evidence.codeqlBuild: Managed assets are built before JavaScript extraction so generated libraries remain scanned.
evidence.branch: develop; current 1.2.x does not contain the HTMX integration.
evidence.validationMessages: Cacti formValidate uses the dependency escapeHtml option for title/custom error messages. Browser regression checks initial creation, update, and successful validation; the original setup parses hostile title text as markup in the isolated fixture. No attacker-controlled Cacti title path is established.

alerts.evidence: URL and HTML are distinct history-item fields; serialization loses field-specific taint. Browser save/restore regression.

Current jquery-validation 1.22.1: findByName escapes the attribute selector and returns existing form DOM elements; clean, validationTargetFor and grouped ARIA paths receive those elements, not HTML strings. Browser regression covers hostile field names, all four paths, and preserved ARIA. This conclusion is scoped to the reported selector/element sinks, not message rendering or arbitrary plugin options.
alerts.resolution: Replace ownership/static-rule rationale with DOM-element and escaped-selector evidence; independent message HTML boundary hardened in formValidate with escapeHtml=true.

alerts.evidence: jsTree edit() keeps h2 as the internally constructed rename-input jQuery object; the outside-click handler wraps that same object and triggers blur. Cacti ctree already enables core.force_text=true. Browser coverage reads that actual configuration and verifies markup-like rename text survives outside-click blur without becoming HTML. Scoped to this reported h2 sink and current Cacti editor, not arbitrary plugin rendering.
alerts.resolution: Replace ownership-only dismissal with controlled rename-input evidence and existing force_text/browser coverage in PR #8298.

alerts.resolution: Replace ownership-only dismissal with sibling DOM evidence and browser coverage in PR #8298.

alerts.coreReview: Core color.php calls $(#hex).colorpicker() with defaults. Input .val() is parsed into a Color object; it does not provide size, regional labels or template options. Browser regression checks hostile input and valid hex round-trip. The reported templates include configurable size/regional values, so plugin-provided configuration and overrides remain unverified; this does not establish a globally safe library boundary.
